Source: A 27-year-old nurse presents to the emergency department with a 30-minute history of palpitations and chest pain.
Her temperature is 98.6°F (37.0°C), blood pressure is 110/72 mmHg, pulse is 110/min, and respirations are 11/min.
She has been experiencing nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea after eating leftovers 2 days ago.
Venous blood gas shows a pH of 7.52.
Physical examination is notable for dry mucous membranes and tachycardia with regular rhythm.
She has a history of major depressive disorder for which she takes escitalopram.
Her husband tells the physician that he is concerned that the patient has been increasingly obsessed about her weight recently.
